newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thai foreign minister in Vietnam to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Thai foreign minister in Vietnam to boost ties.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Vietnam and Thailand agreed on Wednesday to step up economic cooperation between their two countries and to resolve long-running disputes over maritime territory.

"We have discussed economic cooperation and Thai investment in Vietnam," Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam told reporters after a meeting in Hanoi with his Thai counterpart, Prachuab Chaiyasarn.
Vietnam and Thailand, both members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), have growing economic links.
Thailand is the ninth-biggest investor in Vietnam, having committed around $1 billion for 72 projects. Two-way trade between the countries was around $620 million in 1996.

However, the two have not always seen eye to eye on potentially oil-rich maritime territory. Scores of fishermen from both Vietnam and Thailand have in the past been arrested for fishing in the other country's waters.
The foreign ministry said last week that all fishermen being detained in both Vietnam and Thailand had now been released.
Prachuab signed an agreement with Cam on bilateral cooperation in science and technology before meeting Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi.
Prachuab's visit, which aimed to lay the groundwork for a visit by Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh later this month, will end in Ho Chi Minh City on Friday.
